messages.snippet: Dear Sarah, We have a serious problem with one of our contract API suppliers, Tessaract Bioreagents,
messages.subject: Defective API batch — potential claim against Tessaract Bioreagents
messages.plaintextBody:
Dear Sarah,

We have a serious problem with one of our contract API suppliers, Tessaract Bioreagents, and would like to instruct Whitfield Carter.

In short: a batch of HX-218 API (TX-HX218-0461) they certified as compliant turned out to contain an out-of-spec impurity. It wrecked a clinical manufacturing lot. Our investigation, now backed by an independent lab, traces the impurity to Tessaract swapping a starting-material supplier without telling us — no change control at all. Stephen (CSO) has the technical detail.

Our exposure is already north of £3m once you count the wasted campaign, replacement API and the knock-on clinical delay. There is a £250k liability cap in the supply agreement which we will obviously want to get round.

Can we set up a call this week?

Kind regards,
Naomi Adeyemi
General Counsel & Company Secretary, Hartwell Pharma

messages.snippet: Dear Naomi, Thank you — we would be glad to act. This sounds like a strong breach-of-contract claim,
messages.subject: RE: Defective API batch — potential claim against Tessaract Bioreagents
messages.plaintextBody:
Dear Naomi,

Thank you — we would be glad to act. This sounds like a strong breach-of-contract claim, and the change-control point is potentially the key that unlocks the cap (most well-drafted caps carve out deliberate breach, and on the face of it that is what you have).

To get us started, please could Stephen send the supply agreement (with the quality agreement and Schedule 3), the CoA for the batch, the OOS investigation, and the Wraysbury report. I'll bring in Tom Gallagher as senior associate.

I have time Thursday at 2pm or Friday morning. Shall we say Thursday?

Kind regards,
Sarah

--
Whitfield Carter LLP, 22 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4BQ
Confidential and may be legally privileged.
